changes.old: Larabanga’s historic mosque is a landmark of northern Ghana’s Islamic architectural heritage.
changes.description: Larabanga Mosque is an earthen religious building in the Sudanic architectural tradition. Its buttresses, projecting timber and towers illustrate the mosque architecture described by Ghana’s heritage authorities. “Historic Sudanic architectural heritage” is covered here as architectural context, not a separate trip stop.

changes.old: Assin Manso. A remembrance destination inland, requiring a separate trip plan.
changes.description: The Assin Manso Ancestral Slave River Park commemorates people forced along the transatlantic slave-trade route. Assin South District Assembly identifies the Last Bath river site, the Memorial Wall of Return and the Ancestral Graveyard within this same park. The memorial and burial grounds are included in this listing rather than counted as separate trip stops.

changes.description: The Komfo Anokye Sword Site stands on the grounds of Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi. Ghana Tourism Authority presents the sword and its associated traditions as part of Asante history. Accounts of the sword’s immovability are traditional beliefs, not claims independently verified by Tourism Compass.

changes.description: Cape Coast is an historic Oguaa city in Ghana’s Central Region. Its castle, market and traditional cultural life provide different perspectives on the city’s history. The Metropolitan Assembly presents these as parts of the wider town experience, rather than one gated attraction.

changes.old: A historic fortification site with traces of former structures, rather than an intact castle attraction.
changes.description: Fort Frederiksborg at Amanful is a historic fort site in Cape Coast, distinct from Fort Gross Friedrichsburg at Princestown. Ghana Museums and Monuments Board includes the Amanful fort in its inventory. The exact visible remains and a suitable visitor access point have not been verified; this is not presented as an intact castle.
